title: Layout: Lines, Groups, Children and Tabs
summary: SameLine, Indent, groups, item widths, child regions, collapsing headers, tab bars and a clean two-column property grid for an engine Inspector.

options: Adds 120 pixels of space after the previous widget
Places the next widget on the same line, starting at x = 120 from the window's left edge
Makes the next widget 120 pixels wide
Indents the rest of the window by 120 pixels
quiz.explain: The first argument is an absolute X offset (in window coordinates). The second argument, spacing, is the gap after the previous item. SameLine(0, 20) means 'right after the last item, 20 px gap'.

quiz.q: You want a slider to fill all the remaining width of the current column or window. Which call do you make before it?
quiz.explain: Negative widths mean 'align this many pixels from the right edge'. -FLT_MIN is the smallest negative number, so the widget stretches to the right edge with no label space left over.

quiz.q: Which call must be matched with EndChild() even if it returned false?
quiz.explain: BeginChild/EndChild behave like Begin/End: always paired. BeginTabBar and BeginTabItem only need their End call when they returned true, and CollapsingHeader needs no end call at all.

quiz.q: Why call AlignTextToFramePadding() before a Text() that sits next to a slider?
options: So the text baseline lines up with the framed widget's text instead of sitting higher
It is required before every Text()
quiz.explain: Framed widgets (sliders, inputs, buttons) have vertical padding. Plain text doesn't. AlignTextToFramePadding pushes the text down by FramePadding.y so both line up.
